title: Foundation daemon ingress surface
description: Objective: publish the committed Foundation command/read surfaces so an external canary or MCP host can drive production authority without deep imports or reimplementing ingress. Deliverable: a focused curated area surface plus @moe/daemon root exports for review schema/kinds/refusal vocabularies and runReviewCommand/readReviewLedger; durable restart reconciliation/continuation; Foundation attempt/verification services and read models; review-qualified closure; and coordination adapter operations, with full type closure. NOT in scope: behavior changes, fixtures, transport listeners, or new authority. Depends on Recovery continuation evidence binding, Durable Claude attempt dispatch, Durable verification receipt dispatch, Review-qualified goal closure, and Daemon coordination authority adapter. apps/daemon/src/index.ts is already 249 lines: extract a focused `apps/daemon/src/foundation/foundation-surface.ts` with explicit named exports and keep every production file <=250 rather than growing index.ts past target. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/index.ts, index-surface.test.ts, runtime-entrypoint.test.ts, and apps/daemon/src/foundation/foundation-surface.ts/.js. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck plus a plain-Node root probe from apps/daemon.
definitionOfDone: @moe/daemon root exposes executable review, recovery, attempt, verification, closure, and coordination entrypoints plus their runtime schema/kind/reason vocabularies and complete type-only closure; no test fixture or export-star leak appears in the curated area surface.
Package-root tests use @moe/daemon and exact namespace set equality to catch both missing and unreviewed runtime exports, while type assertions distinguish every public result branch.
A plain Node import from apps/daemon resolves every entrypoint and invokes safe decode/read probes without Vitest's .js-to-.ts remapping.
apps/daemon/src/index.ts and the new focused production surface each remain <=250 physical lines; no behavior module or package manifest changes.
Daemon focused tests/typecheck and repo typecheck exit 0 with test count at least baseline, and only the five owned paths are committed.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.
Curate explicit named exports in the area module; package-root runtime set equality must prevent fixtures or incidental helpers from leaking.

Assert EXACT SET EQUALITY over the runtime namespace -- both directions, so the test catches a missing export AND an unreviewed one that leaked in. - COORDINATION: all four mailbox operations' return types, adapter options, digest signature.

SOURCES, all present: review-services.ts (runReviewCommand), review-ledger.ts (readReviewLedger), recovery/restart-reconciliation.ts (reconcileOnRestart), recovery/continuation-command.ts (runContinuationCommand), work/foundation-attempt-service.ts, evidence/foundation-verification-service.ts, coordination/coordination-adapter.ts. TESTS: index-surface.test.ts is 851 lines and is where the set-equality guard belongs; runtime-entrypoint.test.ts is 213 lines and is where the plain-Node probe belongs. A new .ts module needs its one-line .js bridge or it is invisible to the .js import graph -- and Vitest's .js-to-.ts remapping HIDES a missing bridge inside the suite, which is precisely why DoD 3 demands a real Node process. NOTE: createCoordinationAdapter still has no production caller; publishing it is this task's job and does not conflict with the canary's separate descope of the coordination gap.
planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is a set-equality test that cannot fail: derive the expected namespace from the module at runtime and it agrees with any export list forever. It must be a frozen hand-written literal, asserted in BOTH directions (missing and leaked) with a size assertion, and drills 1 and 2 exist because a single-direction assertion catches only one of the two failures. Second risk is the plain-Node probe collapsing into an ordinary vitest import: inside the worker, .js-to-.ts remapping resolves a module whose bridge does not exist, so the probe must spawn a real node process -- drill 3 proves it by deleting a bridge and requiring the probe to redden while the in-suite tests stay green. Third, incomplete type closure: an exported function whose refusal union is unexported typechecks in-package and fails at the consumer, so export every branch a caller must narrow on. Fourth, the graph-preview extraction must keep every existing consumer import path working -- re-export from index.ts; a moved export that changes a consumer's path IS a behavior change, which this task forbids. Verify the move at its ORIGIN too, or a symbol defined in both files drifts later. Fifth, CONCURRENCY: a prior handoff recorded another task in flight against index.ts and index-surface.test.ts, two owned paths, in one shared working directory -- check `git log` on those files and re-read before committing. Sixth, DoD 5 requires the test count to be at least baseline, so capture the baseline BEFORE the first edit; afterwards it is unrecoverable. Finally, this is a publishing task: no behavior module changes, no manifest changes, no new authority -- if the surface appears to need one, that is a finding to report, not a line to add.
